findings.claim: Mouse SLC29A1 contains amino acid substitutions E72A and N74S that convert the human PERN sequence to PARS in the mitochondrial-targeting region.
findings.mechanism: The N-terminal PEXN sequence is implicated in human ENT1 mitochondrial targeting, and substitution to PAXS causes loss of mitochondrial localisation, meaning mitochondrial transport and associated toxicity observed in humans may not occur in mice.
findings.scepticNote: The sequence alignment verifies the E72A and N74S substitutions within the putative targeting motif, but sequence divergence alone does not directly demonstrate altered mitochondrial localization or transport activity in vivo.

findings.claim: Human ENT1 possesses an identified mitochondrial targeting signal reported to explain interspecies differences in fialuridine toxicity, whereas mouse localisation is assigned only to cell membranes by similarity.
findings.mechanism: If mouse ENT1 lacks the mitochondrial localisation of the human protein, mitochondrial accumulation of transported substrates will not occur in the animal model, masking human mitochondrial toxicity.
findings.scepticNote: Contrasting curated human literature against mouse UniProt annotations transferred by similarity relies on an incomplete layer and does not establish biological absence of mouse ENT1 from mitochondria.

findings.claim: SLC29A1 is detected in 2.01% of human endothelial cells of hepatic sinusoid compared to 80.51% of mouse endothelial cells of hepatic sinusoid.
findings.mechanism: Higher expression of SLC29A1 in mouse sinusoidal endothelial cells could result in altered hepatic extraction, drug clearance, or disposition compared to humans.
findings.scepticNote: Single-cell RNA detection percentages from unnormalized, aggregated datasets reflect assay conditions and differing cell-type annotations rather than verified differences in cell-level protein expression.
